title: Fifty years, 36 moments
lede: From half a bar in Richfield to one restaurant in St. Louis Park. Filter by thread.

events.title: The first restaurant
events.text: Marno McDermott opens Chi-Chi’s in half of Max McGee’s Left Guard bar in Richfield, Minnesota. Sources give 1975 or 1976.

events.title: Shelly Frank and Louisville
events.text: Frank leaves Kentucky Fried Chicken to run the company for John Stephens & Co., which holds the franchise rights. Headquarters move to Louisville.

events.title: Profit of $9.1M
events.text: Company-owned restaurants have gone from one to 46 in two years, by a reference history’s account.

events.title: Peak profit
events.text: Net income reaches $16.7M, the highest the reference history records.

events.title: 42 openings in a year
events.text: 27 company-owned and 15 franchised restaurants open.

events.title: Hal Smith takes over
events.text: Frank retires. The chain has 200 restaurants and falling profits.

events.title: Foodmaker buys the chain
events.text: The owner of Jack in the Box pays about $235M.

events.title: Best year for sales
events.text: Sales of $450M, as a reference history gives them.

events.title: Smith quits
events.text: He cites personal reasons. Two presidents follow within a year.

events.title: Consul bought out of Chapter 11
events.text: Chi-Chi’s pays $8.7M in cash for a major franchisee and keeps 22 of its 26 restaurants.

events.title: Family Restaurants Inc.
events.text: Foodmaker contributes Chi-Chi’s to a new company owned with Apollo and Green Equity Investors. The price is about $270.0M including assumed debt.

events.title: $144.78M written off
events.text: All the goodwill recorded for the Chi-Chi’s merger is written off in its first year.

events.title: A new president
events.text: Roger Chamness joins as president of Chi-Chi’s.

events.title: Sales fall 11.5%
events.text: Comparable-restaurant sales drop 11.5%; the division’s EBITDA is a loss of $4.3M.

events.title: 48 restaurants marked for divestment
events.text: The parent records a provision of $22.9M. Twenty of the 48 are later kept because their leases cannot be ended.

events.title: Prandium
events.text: Family Restaurants renames itself Prandium Inc.

events.title: El Torito sold
events.text: Chi-Chi’s becomes the parent’s largest remaining chain.

events.title: Prandium files Chapter 11
events.text: A pre-packaged plan for the parent and one subsidiary. It is confirmed on June 20 and takes effect on July 2. The operating subsidiaries, including Chi-Chi’s, are not part of it.

events.title: The chief executive resigns
events.text: Kevin S. Relyea leaves. In February 2003 two members of the turnaround firm Alvarez & Marsal take over.

events.title: A $6.4M offer for the parent
events.text: Investors sign a non-binding letter of intent to buy Prandium for $6.4M in cash plus contingent payments. The deal falls apart that summer.

events.title: The exposure
events.text: Most of the patrons who will fall ill eat at the Beaver Valley Mall restaurant in these four days.

events.title: Chi-Chi’s files Chapter 11
events.text: Chi-Chi’s, Inc. and Koo Koo Roo file in Delaware. Chi-Chi’s has a letter of intent from a buyer.

events.title: Prandium deregisters
events.text: The parent files a Form 15 and stops reporting to the SEC. It has about 264 stockholders of record.

events.title: The advisory
events.text: Pennsylvania’s health department issues an advisory and the restaurant closes.

events.title: A third death
events.text: At least 490 people are ill. The chain removes green onions from all its restaurants.

events.title: The CDC names green onions
events.text: A dispatch reports about 555 cases as of November 20 and traces the onions to Mexico.

events.title: Outback wins the auction
events.text: The bankruptcy court approves Outback Steakhouse as bidder for the designation rights to 76 properties, for $42.5M.

events.title: The restaurants close
events.text: The Outback deal closes and Chi-Chi’s ceases operations. Its website says “Adios.”

events.title: The final count
events.text: The CDC’s investigators publish their study: 601 patients, three deaths, at least 124 hospitalised.

events.title: A $6.25M settlement
events.text: A federal judge approves a settlement for a man who needed a liver transplant.

events.title: $162.23 each
events.text: Cheques go out to 4,931 people who received shots, from an $800,000 class settlement. Total settlements pass $40M.

events.title: MegaMex Foods
events.text: Hormel and Herdez Del Fuerte close a 50/50 joint venture whose brands include Chi-Chi’s.

events.title: Luxembourg closes
events.text: The two Chi-Chi’s restaurants in Luxembourg close at the end of a franchise agreement. One had opened in 1989.

events.title: A licence for the founder’s son
events.text: Michael McDermott announces an agreement with Hormel to open Chi-Chi’s restaurants.

events.title: St. Louis Park
events.text: The first new Chi-Chi’s opens at 1602 West End Boulevard.

events.title: No second conversion
events.text: The Rojo Mexican Grill in Maple Grove closes without becoming a Chi-Chi’s; a different site is said to be planned.
